_comment: Rule-engine thresholds, keyed by the RED-LESION MODEL that produced the counts.
WHY KEYED, AND NOT JUST CHANGED. These are not clinical constants. They are
properties of the SEGMENTER: redFloor is a measured false-positive noise
floor, not a number from the ETDRS text. Retrain the lesion model and every
one of them is describing a detector that no longer exists.
Measured: on one image v1 found 31 red lesions and v2 found 81 -- 2.6x. Run
v2's counts through v1's thresholds and referable specificity on IDRiD's
103-image test split collapses to 0.231, i.e. 30 of the 39 non-referable
eyes get flagged. So a threshold set is only meaningful against the counts it
was fitted to, and the two must travel together. That is what this file is:
redLesionModelVersion and hands the rule engine the matching set, so the
pairing cannot come apart by someone flipping one and forgetting the other.
Both engines read it through the same caseRuleOpts(), so the MATLAB rule
engine and the JS fallback cannot drift onto different thresholds.

v1._source: The original hand-measured values, from 14 validation images (ruleEngineGrade.m's header). Left untouched: v1 is no longer the default and re-fitting a retired model's thresholds would be work with no consumer.

v2._source: grading/optimizeRuleThresholds.m, fitted 2026-09-23 on IDRiD's official grading TRAIN split (251 of 413 images on disk) and reported on the untouched TEST split (103/103). Counts from diagnostics/collectLesionCounts.py with RED_LESION_MODEL_VERSION=v2.
_whyGrade3QuadMinIs4Not8: The joint search fitted 8 on TRAIN; Youden's J (perfcurve) and Tanuj's
independent Python fit both said 4. Isolating the parameter settled it:
grade3QuadMin changes NEITHER sensitivity NOR specificity (both flat at
0.859 / 0.872 for every value 3..10) because it only separates grade 3
from grade 2, and both are referable. It moves exact-grade accuracy only:
on TRAIN 8 wins (0.757 vs 0.709), on the held-out TEST 4 wins (0.650 vs
0.602). The held-out number is the honest one, so 8 was overfitting and 4
is kept -- which is also the value two independent methods already agreed on.
_knownLimitations: SENSITIVITY IS BELOW THE 0.90 TARGET. 0.859 held out, and no threshold set
in this family reaches 0.90 with usable specificity -- the frontier tops out
near 0.875. That is a model-level limit, not a tuning choice, and it must be
disclosed rather than tuned around. With 64 referable test cases, 0.875 and
0.90 may not be statistically distinguishable either way.
GRADE 1 IS ESSENTIALLY UNDETECTED: of 17 true grade-1 test cases, 14 are
called 0. Pre-existing, not caused by this refit, but it is in the confusion
matrix and should not be quoted around.
